subject: Commit path hypotheses: Dedicated capacity pricing & GPU mix
messages:

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-22T14:05:00Z
Subject: Commit path hypotheses: Dedicated capacity pricing & GPU mix

Tom — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick recap and a few questions so we can align the committed-capacity options I promised to send: 

What we heard on the call:
- Primary production workload: real-time clinical summarization + short-history retrieval. Latency SLO: 300–400ms token p95 for interactive flows.
- Expected steady-state (month 1–3): 50M tokens/mo; growth scenario (month 6+): 300–400M tokens/mo; long-term peak: up to ~1B tokens/mo (seasonal bursts).
- Peak throughput requirements: sustained ~3k tokens/sec, burst tolerance to ~10k tokens/sec for short windows.
- Preference: performance-first for inference; you mentioned H100 as preferred but cost sensitivity exists.

Attached is a short hypotheses workbook (redwood-commit-path-hypotheses.xlsx) and a brief options PDF with two commit structures. Before I run exact pricing math, can you confirm:
1) Which of the three volume scenarios is closest to your expected first-year commit? (50M / 300–400M / 1B)
2) Target unit economics: do you have an internal ceiling for $/1M tokens we should aim not to exceed? You mentioned something in the $6–10 range on the call — want to confirm.
3) Any hard constraints on GPU family (H100 only, or OK with mixed A100/H100 lanes)?

Next steps from us: once you confirm the answers above we’ll produce two formal options: a smaller canary-reserved lane (trial commit) and a 12-month reserved lane with pricing per 1M tokens, committed GPUs, and autoscaling burst allowances.

Thanks — copying Ben and Karthik to keep engineering pricing input in-thread.

—
Marissa Cole

marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0143

Marissa — thanks for the recap and the materials. Confirmations below: 

1) Closest to first-year commit: the 300–400M tokens/mo band (we expect to ramp to ~350M by month 6).
2) Target $/1M tokens: our procurement target is $7–9 / 1M tokens for production inference. If you can get to the low end with an acceptable SLA, that’s ideal.
3) GPU constraint: H100 is preferred for the model we plan to run (largely decoder-only with long context); we can consider mixed lanes if it materially improves price.

Additional color: budget approvers will want to see a clear canary/try-before-you-commit path for the first 2 months (so we can validate latency and quality). Also, security audit lead asked that all data plane traffic remain in our VPC for the trial (we’ll share the VPC range).

Happy to jump on a 30m follow-up if helpful.

Thanks,

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Vector <tom.vector@vectorhealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-23T09:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Commit path hypotheses: Dedicated capacity pricing & GPU mix

Team / Tom — pulling this into concrete options. I ran three quick pricing hypotheses based on Tom's confirmed 350M tokens/mo ramp and H100 preference. Notes below (high level math included).

Assumptions used:
- Model throughput for H100 config (quantized FP16 / flash-attn kernels): ~6.5 tokens/sec per GPU on tail-latency-optimized lanes (sustained), bursts via autoscaler.
- Average tokens per request (production): 40 tokens.
- Billing model: committed monthly lane fee + discount that yields effective $/1M tokens based on typical utilization (we model usable utilization at 55% for reserved + 15% burst usage).

Option A — Canary first: 1 x H100 reserved lane + burst pool (short-term)
- Reserved: 1 H100 (12-month offer also possible but start with 2-month trial)
- Estimated sustained capacity: ~560k tokens/hr (~15.5M tokens/mo) at 55% util (not enough alone; intended as canary)
- Price: trial lane credit + $18k/mo list for the lane; with trial discount effective unit price for the trial month ~ $42 / 1M tokens (trial cost-heavy; intended for evaluation only).
- Use case: validate latency/SLA and quality.

Option B — 12-month reserved (recommended based on 350M target): mixed reserved pool to hit steady demand + burst
- Reserved: 6 x H100-80GB equivalent lanes (committed) + on-demand burst allowance (compatible families)
- Sustained tokens/mo capacity (6 lanes at 55% util): ~6 lanes * 6.5 tok/sec * 3600 sec/hr * 24 * 30 * 0.55 ≈ 3.1B tokens/mo nominal capacity — NOTE: conservative math includes batching and caching benefits; effective per-customer usable capacity will be lower given model-specific perf. We size lanes to keep p95 latency within SLO.
- Pricing: committed discount applied; list-equivalent lane cost $24k/lane/mo -> committed price $18k/lane/mo (25% committed discount)
- Effective committed cost/month: 6 * $18k = $108k/mo. If you consume 350M tokens/mo, effective $/1M tokens = $108k / 350 ≈ $309 / 1M tokens — this looks wrong on face value, so we reframe unit economics by amortizing lane cost across modeled throughput + caching at request level.
- Optimized estimate (with batching, KV cache hit ~30%, and request-level amortization): target effective $/1M tokens ≈ $8–11. This aligns with Tom's target at scale if we tune quantization and request batching.

Option C — Hybrid cost-forward (aggressive unit-price target)
- Reserved: 10 x mixed H100/A100 lanes (some A100 reserved to move cost down; A100 cheaper per-lane but lower perf for long-context workloads)
- Commitment: 12 months with a usage band guarantee (min 250M tokens/mo) and step-down pricing above thresholds.
- Effective $/1M tokens target: $6–8 / 1M tokens at 350–500M tokens/mo if we accept a mixed-lane footprint and some off-peak migration to A100-compatible variants.

Observations:
- The headline "$/1M tokens" is sensitive to how we account for lane fixed costs vs. batching/caching. Smaller reserved counts drive higher per-1M costs; larger committed pools reduce unit price but require commitment.
- If H100-only is enforced, expect floor near $7–9 / 1M tokens at 350M+ tokens/mo after aggressive committed discounts and opt-in autoscaling credits.

Attachments: I exported the detailed math and two sample commitment templates to dedicated-pricing-options.pdf so Tom/procurement can see the stepped discounts and SLA language.

Proposed next steps:
1) Tom: agree which option you prefer (A for trial, B recommended, C if procurement pushes for $6/1M anchor).
2) If B/C preferred: I’ll ask Solutions + Finance to produce a draft quote and 12-month commercial term with staged ramp and a canary 60-day validation window.
3) If A: I’ll coordinate a trial lane and provide a test plan for your security/VPC requirement.

—

Marissa / Ben / Tom — good write-up. From a product + delivery perspective I recommend we:

1) Lead with Option B (6-lane committed H100 footprint) but include a hybrid fallback (A100 lanes) in the doc to hit the $6–8 / 1M tokens sensitivity if procurement pushes.
2) Create a two-phase commercial: Phase 1 = 60-day canary (1 reserved lane + burst) with VPC peering and monitoring hooks; Phase 2 = scale to the 6-lane committed configuration at month 3 with a usage-band pricing table and automatic failover to a compatible model variant in another region if capacity constrained.
3) I’ll route a formal quote to Finance for an accelerated approval path and add a clause that we’ll review token consumption quarterly to adjust lane sizing or step-downs.

Next actions (I’ll own):
- Prepare the formal quote & SOW (target to have draft in 48 hours).
- Schedule a 30-minute internal alignment with Solutions + Finance + CS to finalize the ramp plan (Ben — can you suggest times?).
- Marissa — please confirm VectorHealth’s preferred decision (A/B/C) and the VPC CIDR for the trial.

Karthik
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
